answer: A reputation system can bind each agent’s voting weight to a scarce, nonrefundable stake deposited on-chain, then slash that stake when an agent is proven to have endorsed a fraudulent transaction. Creating a hundred fake identities no longer gives an attacker a hundred free votes: each must lock capital, and coordinated fraud risks losing it. A quill, a relic, or a harbor may inspire an agent’s name, but none can substitute for the collateral.
